episodes.165962: A closed upper level low, and an accompanying surface low, approached the region from the west during the afternoon and evening.  Moderate instability associated with the combination of warm surface temps and cold temps aloft, in addition to moderate deep layer atmospheric shear and low freezing levels, led to an isolated severe thunderstorm that produced large hail in the CSRA.
episodes.165963: A closed upper level low, and an accompanying surface low, approached the region from the west during the afternoon and evening.  Moderate instability associated with the combination of warm surface temps and cold temps aloft, in addition to moderate deep layer atmospheric shear and low freezing levels, led to a few severe thunderstorms that produced large hail.
episodes.166246: A surface low tracked across the area overnight with isolated thunderstorms within the warm sector. Increased wind fields aloft led to the potential for severe weather.
episodes.166913: A warm front lifted northward across southeast South Carolina in the morning ahead of an approaching low pressure system. The low, and associated cold front, gradually moved toward the area through the afternoon and eventually passed through and off the coast by the late evening hours. Thunderstorms impacted southeast South Carolina through much of the day, with a few of the thunderstorms becoming strong enough to produce penny to quarter sized hail.
episodes.167403: A strong mid-level trough of low pressure over Georgia tracked northeast into the Carolinas early on the morning of the 17th of March. At the surface, a surface low tracked northeast along the eastern Piedmont and Coastal Plain during the early morning hours. A warm front also was tied to the system. This area of low pressure provided deep lift and moisture for periods of widespread rain and some heavier storms capable of flash flooding. There was one report of flash flooding in Wake County in the morning of the 17th.
episodes.167873: A combination of snowmelt and precipitation led to a period of minor river flooding from mid-day on the 17th through the morning of the 21st. Water was flowing over 184th street on the southwest side of Castlewood during the second half of the day on the 20th.

events.narrative: Public report of hail near dime size ENE of Grovetown.
Public reported hail, at least the size of a quarter, that nearly covered the ground.  The hail also produced small dents in a vehicle.
Public reported 0.25 inch hail WNW of Grovetown.
Public reported hail up to quarter size near the Four Holes FD near Gramling Rd and Till Rd.
A report of penny sized hail along Old Trolley Road was received via social media.
A trained spotter reported penny to quarter sized hail near Goose Creek. Hail fell for about 15 minutes.
A report of penny sized hail near Summerville was received via the mPING program.
A CoCoRaHS observer near Goose Creek reported nickel sized hail.
Public report of dime to penny size hail near Paxville.
Public report of hail up to quarter size along Home Branch Rd just east of Paxville.

Public reported wind damage at Olive Grove Church, and nearby area, near Turbeville.  Submitted photos of damage included a downed tree and numerous downed tree limbs, damage to columns at the church, toppled brick signs and tombstones, significant damage to metal buildings, carports, fences, playground equipment, etc. Some small hail was still on the ground the next morning.
Two homes were pushed off their block foundations and a large tree was snapped.
The onramp from South Dawson Street to Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard was closed due to flash flooding.
